Named after our philosophy of limitless learning and iteration, we specialize in taking complex, high-stakes challenges and engineering clean, efficient, and user-centric applications. summary:
We developed Kshetra (क्षेत्र), an agricultural decision support platform built for smallholder farmers and agricultural extension officers across Ahilya Nagar and Nashik districts in Maharashtra, India. Using interactive satellite parcel mapping (Esri World Imagery) with dual-CRS geodesic validation (WGS84 and UTM Zone 43N), live Open-Meteo weather/FAO-ET0/soil-moisture telemetry, ISRIC SoilGrids 250 m soil properties, and MPKV Rahuri agronomy catalogs, Kshetra turns spatial and climate data into plot-level farm guidance.

Farmers and extension officers receive parcel-scaled FAO-56 daily and weekly irrigation water volumes in liters, 48-hour spray-safety windows, a transparent 0–100 five-factor crop suitability ranker across 16 regional crops, rotation and harvest tracking, printable Devanagari credential cards, an installable offline-capable PWA, and Krishi Mitra — a Marathi, Hindi, and English voice-assisted advisor grounded strictly in the farmer's real parcel data. By displaying data provenance, reporting "No data" instead of guessed zeros, and enforcing India DPDP Act 2023 privacy protections, Kshetra makes scientific farm planning practical on everyday smartphones.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Kshetra connects field extension officers and smallholder farmers through verified spatial land parcels rather than generic district advice:

1. Role-Based Onboarding & Satellite Mapping: Extension officers onboard farmers (capped cleanly at 40 farmers per village cluster and up to 4 parcels per farmer) and trace Gat/Survey farm boundaries on Esri World Imagery, OpenStreetMap, or OpenTopoMap tiles, or import GeoJSON/KML files. The backend validates RFC 7946 polygon orientation, checks Ahilya Nagar / Nashik district containment (across 29 talukas), cross-checks WGS84 geodesic vs. UTM Zone 43N (EPSG:32643) area within <0.5% divergence, and rejects >2% parcel overlaps.

2. Live Earth & Agro-Climate Pipeline: For each parcel centroid, the backend fetches 7-day weather forecasts, 48-hour hourly wind/humidity/rain, 30-day rainfall history, FAO ET0, solar radiation, and 0–7 cm soil moisture from Open-Meteo, plus 250 m soil chemistry (pH, clay, sand, organic carbon, nitrogen) from ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 (with optional Agmarknet/data.gov.in market prices), backed by an SSRF host allowlist, circuit breaker, and SQLite/PostgreSQL snapshot caching.

3. Explainable Precision Agronomy Engine: Rather than a black-box guess, Kshetra computes a transparent 0–100 crop suitability score across 5 weighted factors — Water Match (30), Soil Match (25), Season/Temp Match (20), Duration Efficiency (15), and Rotation Health (10) — across 16 regional crops calibrated to MPKV Rahuri Package of Practices, alongside FAO-56 daily water requirements in liters, Magnus-Tetens dew point, VPD, Growing Degree Days (GDD), Regional Soil Hydration Index (RSHI), and 48-hour pesticide spray safety windows.

4. Krishi Mitra Grounded Assistant & Trilingual Voice: Farmers can ask questions or translate guidance seamlessly across Marathi, Hindi, and English with Web Speech voice input/output. The assistant injects verified plot coordinates, live weather, and suitability scores into optional LLM adapters (Google Gemini / OpenAI / local Ollama) or runs completely offline via a deterministic rule-based agronomy engine.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

- Replaces guesswork irrigation and risky windy/pre-rain spraying with measurable water volumes (liters/day) and 48-hour safe windows, conserving groundwater and input costs.

- Eliminates language barriers for rural farmers with full Marathi, Hindi, and English UI, glossaries (105 terms), voice narration, and printable Devanagari A6 credential cards.

- Prevents hallucinated chemical or financial advice through strict "No data" transparency rules, Integrated Pest Management (IPM) priority, and mandatory Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) verification notices.

- Protects farmer privacy under India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023 with first-login vernacular consent, field-level encryption (enc:v1: Encrypt-then-MAC) for mobile and Gat/survey numbers, Argon2id password hashing, 30-minute HS256 JWT + rotating refresh tokens, and one-click JSON export / account deletion.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE & SOFTWARE USED

- Backend: Python 3.12, Flask 3, Waitress, SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic, SQLite (WAL mode) / PostgreSQL, Shapely 2, PyProj 3 (UTM 43N), Argon2-cffi + PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, Cryptography, PyJWT, ReportLab & qrcode (Devanagari PDF cards & LAN QR codes), Pytest.

- Frontend & Packaging: TypeScript, React 18, Vite 6, Tailwind CSS 3, Leaflet satellite mapping, Recharts, Lucide icons, PWA Service Worker (WebAPK), Capacitor/TWA Android build kit, and a native .NET C# Windows launcher (Kshetra-Desktop.exe).

- Hardware / Accessibility Design: Runs on standard laptops, local village kiosks over Wi-Fi LAN sharing, and low-end Android phones.

CREATIVITY & DESIGN FACTORS (COST, ENERGY, ACCESSIBILITY)

- Zero-Demo Truthfulness: Missing feeds never show misleading "0" values — Kshetra explicitly displays "No data" with source timestamps, enforced automatically by a repository guard script (check_no_demo.py).

- Cost & Bandwidth Efficiency: Built entirely on free/open geospatial and weather APIs (no mandatory paid LLM/satellite keys to operate), 1-hour weather and 24-hour soil caching, Service Worker offline UI caching, and an optional local deterministic AI engine to minimize mobile data and compute energy.

- Accessibility: Devanagari-first interface (Marathi/Hindi/English toggle), voice playback for low-literacy accessibility, and QR-code LAN sharing so farmers need zero manual setup.
